source.title: Connecting Optimization and Generalization via Gradient Flow Path Length
source.authors: Fusheng Liu; Hai-Zhao Yang; Soufiane Hayou; Qianxiao Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation or corruption affecting extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports measured results on quantities related to generalization and optimization paths, and evaluates generalization bounds in neural-network experiments; its methods and measures differ from the claim versions' memorization, test-gap, and architecture comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper numerically estimates Uniform-LGI constants along training paths and compares a derived bound with test error only through a plotted bound; it does not report a numerical training-versus-test error gap. The label-flip results concern Uniform-LGI constants, not held-out error. Reported generalization bounds and cited comparisons are theoretical or prior-work statements, not measured outcomes for the claim versions. Rows record the paper's own neural-network Uniform-LGI estimates and label-flip measurements.
record.test_reason: The study measures Uniform-LGI constants and derives conditional generalization bounds. Neither measures any listed version: label corruption changes optimization constants, architecture comparisons concern those constants, and the overparameterization theorem does not establish decreasing test error with increasing width.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors present empirical evidence for Uniform-LGI along selected training paths and use this condition to derive convergence rates and generalization bounds during training. They claim non-vacuous bounds in their applications, including high-dimensional settings; their experiments do not directly test V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies gradient flow theoretically and uses gradient descent or SGD in numerical checks of Uniform-LGI; it does not reproduce the listed interventions or evaluate the train-test gap claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports a smaller Uniform-LGI exponent for WideResNet-16-8 than ResNet18. For the width-512 two-layer network, increasing label-flip ratio decreases cn,δ and increases θn,δ.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated Uniform-LGI constants converge along the tested neural-network training paths; WideResNet has a smaller exponent than ResNet18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniform-LGI estimates characterize optimization paths and vary across the tested architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing training-label corruption decreases the estimated Uniform-LGI constant and increases its exponent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label corruption changes optimization-path geometry in the tested two-class CIFAR-10 network.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper derives conditional generalization bounds for linear regression, kernel regression and two-layer networks, including an overparameterized NTK setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated distributional and optimization assumptions, optimization-path control yields population-loss bounds.

record.problems: The Uniform-LGI estimates are empirical finite-sample checks and cannot prove the inequality. The label-flip experiment's ratios and values are presented only in a figure, with no exact numbers in the text. The paper does not report direct training-versus-test error gaps for the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No numerical or explicit textual outcome directly measures any of the eight versions. The generalization-bound evaluation in Figure 3(b) is a bound, not a reported training-test gap; other theoretical bounds, cited prior results, and loss/optimizer setup details do not meet the row criteria.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance held-out accuracy for random labels.
Test-error changes as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps and comparative ranking performance.
Held-out accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 3(b) plots a bound expression up to a constant, rather than a measured test-error or generalization-gap comparison. Its decrease with sample size supplies no verdict on the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of natural-label and random-label training fit and held-out accuracy.
No width sweep measuring test error past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance comparison.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance.
No dropout intervention or held-out error comparison.
No measurement of magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison with gap rankings.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: two-layer multilayer perceptron (MLP) with width 100 (no bias)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with SGD; estimated Uniform-LGI constants along the optimization path.
rows.measure: Estimated Uniform-LGI exponent θ* and constant c*
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over 10 independent runs
rows.note: The measured quantities characterize the loss along the training path, not the training-test gap.
rows.check: The reported constants match Table 1, but they measure optimization-path geometry rather than any listed claim's effect.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with SGD; estimated Uniform-LGI constants along the optimization path.
rows.measure: Estimated Uniform-LGI exponent θ* and constant c*
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over 10 independent runs
rows.note: The paper reports that θ and c converge and the Uniform-LGI holds along the optimization path.
rows.check: The reported constants match Table 1. Low training loss and Uniform-LGI estimates alone cannot establish any listed generalization comparison.

rows.subject: WideResNet-16-8
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with SGD; estimated Uniform-LGI constants along the optimization path.
rows.measure: Estimated Uniform-LGI exponent θ* and constant c*
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over 10 independent runs
rows.note: The paper notes that increasing ResNet18 width and depth to Wide-ResNet gives a smaller exponent, close to 1/2; this is not a measured test-gap result.
rows.check: The reported constants match Table 1. A smaller Uniform-LGI exponent in WideResNet does not measure V2's test-error trend or V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: two-layer fully connected neural network (no bias) with width m = 512, ReLU activation
rows.operation_detail: Trained after flipping training labels at varying ratios; estimated Uniform-LGI constants.

conditions.value: CIFAR10, first two classes (airplane versus automobile), 10000 training images
different ratio; exact ratios are figure-only
no weight decay, dropout or batch normalization

rows.measure: Estimated Uniform-LGI constants cn,δ and θn,δ
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation over 5 independent runs
rows.note: Text states that as label-flip ratio increases, cn,δ decreases and θn,δ increases. The result is not a held-out error measurement.
rows.check: The text reports decreasing c and increasing θ with label corruption, but no corresponding natural-versus-random-label training-fit and held-out-accuracy comparison. The partial state is therefore unwarranted. Appendix A also specifies stopping at training loss below 0.001 or 20000 epochs.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
